en: The Philippine eagle, known locally as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and is endemic to the forests of Mindanao.
Sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, serves as the highest court and holds the judicial branch of government.
The Ifugao people built the famous Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera mountains over two thousand years ago using stone walls.
During the Sinulog Festival in Cebu, devotees dance in the streets to honor the Santo Niño, or Holy Child Jesus.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian accepted to Harvard Medical School and founded the first pediatric hospital in Manila.
Filipino, based primarily on Tagalog, and English are the two official languages used in the Philippine government and schools.
Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of Spanish friars in the Philippines.
The water buffalo, locally called the carabao, is the national animal of the Philippines and plows rural rice fields.
Jeepneys, originally made from leftover American military jeeps after World War II, are the most popular public utility vehicles in the Philippines.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is visibly shown when neighbors carry a whole nipa hut to help a family relocate.
